info.title: ImagenHub API
info.description: API services with API key authentication and credit-based usage limits

get.description:
Returns basic info about the authenticated API key and user tier.
Useful for testing API key authentication and checking credit/rate limit status.

X-RateLimit-Limit-Minute.description: Request limit per minute (free tier only)

X-RateLimit-Limit-Day.description: Request limit per day (free tier only)

post.summary: Host an image for use in later generations
post.description:
Turn raw image bytes into a hosted reference a generation can consume.

Send exactly one of `file` (multipart), `image_base64`, or `image_url`.
Sending none or more than one is rejected.

The decoded upload limit is 10 MB for every transport.

For a large image, or from a network whose route to this API is slow,
the two-call upload starting at `POST /images/upload-url` sends the
bytes straight to storage instead and returns the same reference.

**The reference is `path`, not `url`.** Persist `path` and send it back
as an image input to `/process`, `/run/{model_name}`, or a template's
`default_inputs`. `url` renders the image now and is a convenience only.

**Uploads expire.** An upload is staging for inference, not storage:
the bytes are removed once the retention window in `expires_at` passes,
whether or not anything still references them. Keep your own original
and upload again rather than treating this as a file store. Saving the
path into a template is the exception — a template copies the image
into permanent storage when it is saved.

Uploaded images are re-encoded to JPEG, PNG or WebP, resized so the
longest edge is at most 4096 pixels, and stripped of metadata. The
stored bytes will therefore differ from what was sent, and `size_bytes`
reports what was stored. Send `path`, never `url`, as the generation
reference.

file.description:
The image file. Accepted formats are JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF,
HEIC, HEIF and AVIF, decided by inspecting the bytes rather
than the filename or declared content type. SVG is rejected.
Maximum 10 MB.

image_base64.description:
Base64-encoded image, with or without a `data:<mime>;base64,`
prefix. Note base64 inflates the payload by about a third and
the 10 MB limit applies to the decoded bytes.

image_url.description:
Public `https://` URL the server fetches. Must be reachable
without credentials; plaintext `http://` is rejected, as are
URLs resolving to private, loopback or link-local addresses.

422.description:
The upload was refused. The message names the reason: an
unsupported or unreadable format, a file over the size or pixel
limit, a URL that could not be fetched, more or fewer than one mode
supplied, or the account's upload quota being full.

post.summary: Mint a URL to upload an image straight to storage
post.description:
The first half of a two-call upload that sends the bytes to storage
directly rather than through this API. The bytes go raw rather than
base64, and they take the caller's own route to the storage bucket
instead of the route to this API, which from some networks is many
times faster.

The response names an `upload_url`, the `headers` the PUT must carry
unchanged, and the `path` the bytes will occupy. PUT the raw image
bytes to `upload_url` with those headers. When the PUT answers 2xx,
send `path` to `POST /images/confirm`, which validates the image and
returns the same reference `POST /images` returns.

Nothing exists until confirmation. Minting creates no row and consumes
no quota; a URL nobody writes to, and bytes nobody confirms, are swept
with the rest of the expiring prefix. The URL writes to one key and
nothing else, until `expires_at`, so a leaked URL can put bytes in one
place that nothing reads until this account confirms them.

This route has its own rate limit, separate from `POST /images` and
from `POST /images/confirm`, so one mint and one confirm never exhaust
either.

422.description:
No slot was minted. Either the account's upload quota is full, or
this deployment cannot sign upload URLs, in which case the message
says to use `POST /images` instead.

post.summary: Turn bytes written to a minted URL into a hosted image
post.description:
The second half of a two-call upload. Send the `path` that
`POST /images/upload-url` returned, once the PUT to its `upload_url`
has answered 2xx.

The bytes are read from storage and treated exactly as bytes sent to
`POST /images`: validated by inspecting them, re-encoded, and given a
new `path` under the same rules. The answer has the same shape as
`POST /images`, and the `path` in it is the reference to keep. The
staged path is consumed and cannot be confirmed twice.

Whatever was at the staged path is removed whether or not it was
accepted, so a refused upload has to be minted and sent again.

422.description:
The upload was refused. The message names the reason: nothing this
account staged is readable at that path (never written, already
confirmed, or staged for another account, which are deliberately
one message), an unsupported or unreadable format, a file over the
size or pixel limit, or the account's upload quota being full.

get.description: Returns all visible AI models with their input schemas.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: Free-text search on model name and display name

get.summary: Get a specific AI model by owner + name
get.description:
Canonical lookup using the (owner, name) pair. Same response shape as
`/models/{aiModel}`. Model names may contain a `/edit` variant suffix,
which is captured as part of `{name}` (e.g. `/models/openai/gpt-image-1/edit`).

Returns visible model-provider combinations. Use query parameters
to filter by provider or model.

post.description:
Submit an image generation request using either a model or a template.
Exactly one of `model_id` or `template_id` must be provided — they are
mutually exclusive.

When using `template_id`, the template's default inputs are merged with
the provided inputs (user input takes priority). The model is resolved
from the template automatically.

Returns a task resource. Poll `GET /tasks/{id}` or stream
`GET /tasks/{id}/stream` (SSE) for status updates and output.

model_id.description: AI model ID. Required if template_id is not provided.

template_id.description: Template UUID. Required if model_id is not provided.

provider_id.description: Provider ID. Optional — system selects default if omitted.

_variables.description:
Values for prompt variables (`{{placeholders}}`) defined on the template.
Keys are variable names; values are strings. Substituted into all string
inputs at job execution time. Missing values fall back to the variable's
`default`; required variables without a value cause a 422 error.

webhook_url.description:
Where to POST the result once the task finishes, instead of polling
for it.

Omit it and we use the default endpoint configured for your
organization, if there is one. Send it as `null` to suppress the
callback for this task even when a default is set.

Must be `https` and must not embed credentials
(`https://user:pass@host` is rejected). Reserved: it is never passed
to the model as a generation input.

metadata.description:
Your own labels for this task: an order number, a campaign, the
customer it belongs to. They are stored with the task, come back
on the task resource, and `GET /tasks` can filter on them.

At most 25 keys. Every value must be a scalar (string, number,
boolean or null), and a string value is capped at 500 characters.
Sending `{}` reads as sending nothing, and the task comes back with
`metadata: null`. Reserved: it is never passed to the model as a
generation input.

additionalProperties.description:
Dynamic input fields defined by the model's input schema.
Keys and types vary per model.

value.prompt: A cat wearing a top hat
A product photo on white background

withTemplateVariables.summary: Process with template_id and prompt variables
withTemplateVariables.description:
The template's prompt is `"A {{style}} illustration of {{product}} on a clean background"`.
Values from `_variables` are substituted into the final prompt sent to the provider.

403.description: Refused. As application/problem+json, the account cannot cover the run (see https://docs.imagenhub.ai/errors/insufficient-credits). As application/json, not authorized to use the specified template.

422.description: Validation error (e.g. both model_id and template_id provided)

post.summary: Clone a design from a product image
post.description: Reproduces the design shown in the source image as a print-ready file. Runs a fixed pipeline — auto-crop the mockup to the printed design, generate, upscale, remove background, resize to a print canvas — on pre-configured defaults; every field except `image` is optional. A run is refused (422) when no printed design can be located in the image, and 503 when design detection is temporarily unavailable. The created task (and each chain step under it) carries `metadata: {"action": "clone"}`, so a design run is filterable and distinguishable from an ordinary /api/process task in the same list. Asynchronous: returns the root task; poll GET /tasks/{id}.

422.description: Validation error (unknown field, ineligible model, malformed resize), or no printed design could be located in the image.

post.description: Generates a new variation of the design shown in the source image as a print-ready file. Same pipeline and contract as /batch/design/clone — including the task carrying `metadata: {"action": "redesign"}` — only the pre-configured prompt differs.

post.summary: Locate the printed design in a mockup
post.description: Standalone detection, without starting a run: returns the printed design's bounding box (box_2d, 0-1000, y-first), clockwise tilt (rotation_degrees), confidence, and — when the detection is trusted — a stored upright crop of the design (crop_path, usable as the `image` of a later design run, plus a temporary crop_url). A distrusted detection returns 200 with fallback=true and the reason. The source image is never modified. 422 when the source cannot be read or exceeds 20MB / 40 megapixels; 503 when detection is temporarily unavailable.

image.description: Source image: a hosted `path` from POST /images (preferred), an https URL, or a data URI.

422.description: The source image could not be read, or exceeds 20MB / 40 megapixels.

post.description:
Submit a generation request by specifying the model by name in the URL path.
The job is queued and processed asynchronously. The provider is selected
automatically.

Returns a task resource immediately. Poll `GET /tasks/{id}` or stream
`GET /tasks/{id}/stream` (SSE) for status updates and output.

Model names may contain slashes (e.g. `black-forest-labs/flux-schnell`).

parameters.description: The model's name. May contain slashes.

Must be `https` and must not embed credentials
(`https://user:pass@host` is rejected).

Reserved out of the model's input namespace, along with
`metadata`: both are stripped before the body is matched against
the model's input schema, and neither reaches the provider.

post.description:
Submit a generation request and wait for it to complete before returning.
Returns the output image URLs and task ID directly in the response.

Use this for low-latency integrations where polling is not practical.
For long-running models, prefer the async `POST /run/{model_name}`.
The provider is selected automatically.

Model names may contain slashes (e.g. `black-forest-labs/flux-schnell`).

`webhook_url` is not accepted here and returns 422 — the result comes back
in this response, so there is nothing to call back about. Use the async
`POST /run/{model_name}` for a callback.

parameters.description: The model's name. May contain slashes.

Your own labels for this task: an order number, a campaign, the
customer it belongs to. Accepted here as well as on the async
endpoint — this response carries only the images, so read them
back with `GET /tasks/{task}` or filter on them in `GET /tasks`.

At most 25 keys. Every value must be a scalar (string, number,
boolean or null), and a string value is capped at 500 characters.

Reserved out of the model's input namespace: stripped before the
body is matched against the model's input schema, and never
forwarded to the provider.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's tasks, most recent first. Filter by
status, template, model, or the labels you attached at creation to review
a batch. Returns a lightweight projection — use `GET /tasks/{task}` for a
task's inputs and output image URLs.

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description:
Filter by the labels attached to the task when it was created. Name one
label per bracketed key, as in `?metadata[partner]=teeinblue`, and repeat
the parameter to narrow further: every pair given has to match, so
`?metadata[partner]=teeinblue&metadata[campaign_id]=cmp_9921` returns only
the tasks carrying both. A pair whose value is empty is skipped rather
than matched on.

get.description:
Returns the current status of a task. When status is `success`,
the `output` field contains signed URLs to generated images
(valid for 1 hour).

Streams a single output image of a successful task as a file
download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). Use `index` to pick
among multiple outputs (default `0`).

parameters.description: Zero-based index of the output image to download

404.description: Task or output image not found

get.description:
Server-Sent Events stream for real-time task status updates.
Each event contains a JSON-encoded task object. The stream
closes when the task reaches `success` or `error` status.

Every category the authenticated account owns, ordered by name. Categories

post.description:
Creates a category owned by the authenticated account. The name must be
unique within the account, compared without regard to case, so "Portrait"
and "portrait" are the same category. Punctuation and diacritics are part

(compared without regard to case), reported under `name`; or the account
is at its category limit, reported under `limit` — a key no field is
bound to, because the fault is with the account rather than the name.
The limit is a deployment setting, not a fixed number.

compared without regard to case.

The templates themselves are untouched, and the name becomes available again.

post.summary: Task finished (sent by us, to you)
post.description:
Sent to the `webhook_url` you supplied on the generation request, once the
task reaches a terminal state. You do not implement a path here — this is
the request we make to whatever URL you gave us.

### Verifying

Deliveries follow the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/)
specification, so you can verify them with an off-the-shelf library rather
than implementing the signature yourself. Libraries exist for JavaScript,
Python, Go, Ruby, Java, C#, Rust, Elixir and PHP.

```php
$wh = new \StandardWebhooks\Webhook($secret);   // whsec_... from your dashboard
$event = $wh->verify($requestBody, $requestHeaders);
```

The signature covers `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`. Reject
anything whose timestamp is more than five minutes old — the library does
this for you.

During a secret rotation, `webhook-signature` carries more than one
space-separated signature and any of them matching is valid. Nothing in your
code needs to change for that; the library already handles it.

### Delivering

Retried up to 6 times — after 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h and 6h — until your endpoint
answers `2xx`. Anything else, including a redirect, counts as a failure and
is retried; we do not follow redirects.

Delivery is **at-least-once and unordered**. The same event may arrive more
than once, so treat `webhook-id` as an idempotency key and ignore an id you
have already processed.

Answer quickly — we time out after 10 seconds — and do the work
asynchronously rather than while we wait.

**Do not depend on delivery.** Endpoints go down and retry budgets run out.
Poll `GET /tasks/{id}` for anything you were expecting and have not heard
about.

### What this describes

The payload is a snapshot of the task at the moment it finished, not a live
view. It is accurate when sent and stays as sent through every retry. For the
current state of a task — at any point, including long after the callback —
follow `data.url` or call `GET /tasks/{id}`.

Both are given deliberately. Read the body and act immediately, or follow the
link and be certain; whichever suits your integration.

`data.output` lists every result the task produced. A task produces a handful
of images at most, and we will not inline more than 100 in a single delivery
— beyond that, read them from `data.url`.

### Changes

Fields are only ever added, never removed and never changed in type, so
there is no version to pin. Ignore fields you do not recognise.

parameters.name: webhook-id
parameters.description: Unique per event and stable across retries. Use it to deduplicate.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds at which this attempt was signed.

parameters.name: webhook-signature
parameters.description:
One or more space-separated `v1,<base64>` signatures. More than one
appears only while a secret is being rotated; any match is valid.

id.description: Same value as the `webhook-id` header, repeated here so it survives a proxy that strips headers.

type.description: Branch on this. More types may be added later.

occurred_at.description:
When the task finished — not when this attempt was sent. A retry
hours later still reports the moment the work completed, which is
what lets you order a burst of events that arrive together after a
backlog clears.

data.description: Every key is always present, null where it does not apply.

url.description:
The task resource. Follow it for authoritative current state,
or ignore it and act on this payload — both are supported.

post_processing_status.description:
`failed` when a post-processing step failed on a run that still
produced an image. The event is still `task.succeeded`, because
you did get output — this is how you learn it is not the output
you asked for.

error.description: Why it failed. Null on success.

2xx.description:
Any 2xx marks the delivery as landed and stops the retries. Anything else
is retried until the budget is spent.

apiKeyAuth.description: API key (sk_igh_...) obtained from the dashboard

ProblemDetails.description: An RFC 9457 problem details object, sent as application/problem+json. `type` identifies the problem and is the URL of its documentation page; members beyond the five listed are specific to the type.

detail.example: Your current balance is 3 credits, but this run costs 10.

balance.description: Credit balance when the request was made; negative while overage is in use

cost.description: What the run would have cost

overage_limit.description: How far below zero the account may go; 0 when overage is off

example.title: Insufficient credits
example.detail: Your current balance is 3 credits, but this run costs 10.

path.description:
The durable reference. This is what to store and what to send back
as an image input. It is not a URL and is not fetchable directly.

url.description:
A URL that renders the image now. For convenience only — do not
persist it in place of `path`.

size_bytes.description:
Size of the stored image. This is what was stored after re-encoding,
so it will usually differ from the size of what was sent.

expires_at.description:
When the bytes are removed. Referencing the image in a generation
does not extend this; the window runs from upload. Saving the path
into a template copies the image somewhere permanent instead.

upload_url.description:
Where to PUT the raw image bytes. The query string carries the
authorization, so no other credential is needed, and nothing else
can be done with it.

headers.description:
Headers the PUT must send unchanged. They are covered by the
signature, so a PUT that drops or edits one is refused by the
bucket. Any `Content-Type` may be sent alongside them: what the
bytes are is decided by inspecting them at confirmation.

path.description:
Where the bytes will land, and what to send to
`POST /images/confirm`. Not an image reference yet, because
nothing has looked at the bytes.

expires_at.description:
When `upload_url` stops accepting a PUT. Ten minutes from minting
by default.

max_bytes.description:
The largest image confirmation will accept. The bucket does not
enforce it, so a larger PUT succeeds and is then refused at
confirmation.

input.description: JSON schema describing model input parameters

owner.description: Publisher / trainer of the model. Slug follows the Replicate convention.

credit_cost.description: Credits charged per generation for this model

personal_access_token_id.description: API key ID used for this task (null if created via JWT)

input.description: Processed input sent to the provider

metadata.description:
Labels attached when the task was created, `null` when none were sent. A
task that runs as a step of a chain carries the labels of the run that
started it.

output.description: Signed URLs to generated images (only present on success)

image.description: Source image: a hosted `path` from POST /images (preferred), an https URL, or a data URI (data:image/png;base64,…). Up to 20MB and 40 megapixels; a larger source is refused with a 422 rather than processed.

model.description: Generation model name (any visible edit-capable model). Omit for the recommended default.

prompt.description: Your own generation prompt; omit to use the mission's pre-configured prompt.

steps.description: Per-step overrides. `params` are the step model's OWN settings — an upscaler's scale, a matting model's alpha — validated against that model's `input` schema (GET /models/{name}, or the model row in list-models over MCP): a key the schema doesn't declare, or a value that fails it (e.g. an out-of-enum scale), is rejected. Reserved `_`-prefixed keys are never allowed. `resize` has no `params`; its own knobs are `preset`/`width`/`height` below.

params.description: e.g. {"remove_inside": true} if the model declares that field.
e.g. {"scale": 4} if the model declares a scale enum including 4.

resize.description: Pass a preset, or explicit width and height — not both.

rotation_degrees.description: Clockwise tilt of the print from upright, in degrees.

crop_px.description: [top, left, bottom, right] pixel crop in the source.

fallback.description: True when the detection was not trusted; no crop is stored.

crop_path.description: Stored key of the upright crop; usable as a design run's `image`.

crop_url.description: Temporary URL of the crop (about one hour).

prompt.description: The mission's pre-configured generation prompt. Show it to the user for editing and send the edited text back as the run's `prompt` to override it.

default_model.description: First available recommended model; null if none are visible.

user_id.description: Owner user ID, or null for public templates

description.example: Enhance product photos with professional lighting

thumbnail.description: Signed URL to the WebP thumbnail image

default_inputs.description: Pre-filled input values merged with user input at processing time

extra_input.description: Provider-specific extra input overrides, keyed by provider name

prompt_variables.description:
Variable definitions for `{{placeholders}}` used in this template's prompt.
Clients use these to render input controls and validate user values before
sending them as `_variables` to `POST /process`.

categories.description: The account's categories this template is filed under

Category.description:
A label an account files its own templates under. Categories are never
shared: every one belongs to the account that created it, and an account
can only ever see, use or name its own.

name.description: Unique within the account, compared without regard to case.

templates_count.description: Templates currently filed under this category. Returned by `GET /categories` only.

PromptVariable.description:
Definition of a single `{{placeholder}}` in a template's prompt or string inputs.
Substitution happens at job execution time using values from the `_variables` map
on `POST /process`. Values fall back to `default` when omitted; if neither is
provided, the `{{name}}` placeholder is left untouched in the final prompt.

name.description: Placeholder identifier matched against `{{name}}` in template strings

default.description: Default value used when the variable is omitted from `_variables`

TaskSummary.description: Lightweight task representation for listings (excludes inputs and resolved output URLs; use `GET /tasks/{task}` for those)

template_id.description: Template the task was generated from, or null for direct model runs

metadata.description: Labels attached when the task was created, `null` when none were sent

TemplateSummary.description: Lightweight template representation for listings (excludes default_inputs, extra_input, and full model details)

user_id.description: Owner user ID, or null for public templates

description.example: Enhance product photos with professional lighting

thumbnail.description: Signed URL to the WebP thumbnail image

has_variables.description: Whether this template defines any prompt variables (full definitions are returned by `GET /templates/{id}`)

categories.description: The account's categories this template is filed under

CreditTransactionType.description:
Ledger entry type. `generation_charge` and `refund` pair with each task;
the remaining values represent billing events (money in/out).

amount.description: Signed credit amount (positive = added, negative = spent)

balance_after.description: User's credit balance immediately after this entry

metadata.description: Contextual fields (e.g. task_id, model, plan, reason)

message.example: Rate limit exceeded for minute window.

InsufficientCredits.description: The account cannot cover the credit cost of the run. See https://docs.imagenhub.ai/errors/insufficient-credits
